title: Two calendar events clash and the priority rules cannot settle it
when: Two events land at the same time and neither outranks the other (for example two showings of two listings at 2 pm).
steps: Agent 18 (Calendar & Task Management) keeps the first event on the calendar.
It does not put the second one on; it asks the authorized user about the conflict, and tells Agent 06 (Showing Scheduler) the showing was not added.

Agent 06 does not tell that buyer the showing is confirmed. It holds the showing for the authorized user: continue confirms it to the buyer, cancel sends nothing (the authorized user offers another time).
Neither event is moved on its own.
never: Silently move or drop either event.
why: Which appointment gives way is a judgment about clients and relationships. That is for the authorized user.
you_see: A question about the conflict, and the second showing held for the authorized user's continue or cancel.
test: Buyer B1 asks to see listing L1 at 2 pm on October 20; buyer B2 asks to see L2 at the same time. B1 is confirmed; B2 gets no confirmation and is held for the authorized user.

title: A briefing item has no source on record
when: Something in the morning briefing points to a message that is not on the record.
steps: The briefing lists it as a gap, naming the missing source.
Items that rest on real messages are not listed as gaps.
never: Present an item whose source is missing as if it were sound.
why: A briefing item with no record behind it cannot be checked. Saying so keeps the briefing honest.
you_see: A gap listed in the briefing.
test: The test plants a waiting item (an inspection report) whose source message is not on the record, then asks for the briefing.

title: The authorized user's instruction conflicts with a contract deadline
when: The authorized user asks for something to be scheduled at a time that conflicts with a contract deadline (for example a final walkthrough after closing).
steps: Agent 18 holds it and shows the authorized user both: the authorized user's instruction and the deadline.
Nothing is scheduled until the authorized user decides. Continue goes ahead; cancel drops the instruction.
An instruction with no conflict goes straight on the calendar.
never: Act on either the instruction or the deadline before the authorized user decides.
why: A walkthrough after closing is likely a mistake; the system asks rather than guessing which date was meant.
you_see: A held instruction showing the conflict, asking the authorized user to continue or cancel.
test: Closing is October 22. The authorized user asks for the final walkthrough on October 25: held; the authorized user cancels and it is dropped. On another transaction a walkthrough before closing goes on the calendar.

title: An agent asks to move a protected deadline block
when: An agent asks to move a calendar block that protects a contract deadline.
steps: Agent 18 refuses.
Only the authorized user can move it; it tells the authorized user the request was refused.
never: Move a deadline block at an agent's request.
why: Deadline blocks protect contract dates. Only the authorized user's confirmation moves them.
you_see: A question saying the request to move the protected block was refused.
test: A closing deadline is on the calendar. The authorized user relays, as a signed setting, a request from Agent 06 to move it (agents have no route to ask this themselves).

title: A day is overbooked
when: A day has more events than the daily limit (8 in the authorized user's settings).
steps: Agent 18 proposes an order of priority for the day; the authorized user confirms the order.
The event over the limit is not added; Agent 06 holds that showing for the authorized user instead of confirming it to the buyer.
never: Reorder or drop events on its own.
why: When everything cannot happen, the authorized user decides what comes first.
you_see: A question saying the day is at capacity, with a proposed order; the extra showing held for the authorized user's continue or cancel.
test: Nine showings are requested on one day; nine calendar requests reach Agent 18. The ninth is not added: the authorized user is asked, and the ninth buyer gets no confirmation.

title: Two sources give different dates for the same deadline
when: The transaction timeline and a document disagree on a deadline date.
steps: Agent 18 tracks both dates.
It tells the authorized user about the conflict, naming both sources.
The morning briefing lists the conflict.
why: Choosing the later date can make a deadline pass unnoticed. Both stay visible until the authorized user settles it.
you_see: A question about the conflicting dates; the conflict in the briefing.
test: The timeline says the inspection is due October 25; the inspection report says October 22.

title: The authorized user's calendar clashes with a contract deadline
when: A soft item on the authorized user's calendar (for example a showing) falls on the day of a contract deadline.
steps: The deadline outranks the soft item.
Agent 18 proposes moving the soft item and asks the authorized user.
never: Move the deadline to fit the calendar.
why: Showings can move; closing dates cannot.
you_see: A question naming the deadline and the soft items that clash with it.
test: A showing at 10:00 on October 20; closing is also October 20.

title: A recurring task quietly stops happening
when: A task that should repeat shows no completions.
steps: Agent 18 reports the pattern to the authorized user.
never: Treat a quiet calendar as a sign that all is well.
why: A task that silently stopped is a problem nobody sees until it is too late.
you_see: A report about the silent task.

title: It is unclear which time zone a party is in
when: Someone involved may be in a different time zone and it has not been confirmed.
steps: Agent 18 confirms the time zone before scheduling.
why: A closing scheduled in the wrong time zone can miss its window.
you_see: A question confirming the time zone.
